workflow: Scheduling and publishing posts across multiple platforms (dev.to, own blog, Medium) requires manual copy-paste and date coordination.
trigger: Writing a new blog post that needs to be published on a specific date/time.
current_workaround: Using a spreadsheet to track publish dates, manually copying markdown to each platform, and setting calendar reminders.
consequence: Inconsistent publication timing, duplicated effort, and reduced reach due to forgetting to cross-post.

workflow: Manually reviewing all comments for spam, abuse, or off-topic content. No automated moderation rules or AI filtering.
trigger: Whenever a new comment is posted on any article.
current_workaround: Relying on community flagging and manual review of flagged comments, plus periodic scanning of recent comments.
consequence: Spam and toxic comments staying visible for hours, driving away legitimate users and increasing moderator burnout.

workflow: Exporting post-level analytics (views, reactions, comments) manually each month to check performance and report to sponsors.
trigger: End of month reporting or need to evaluate content strategy.
current_workaround: Manually scrolling through the Dashboard, copying numbers into a spreadsheet, and calculating trends.
consequence: Time wasted on data entry, prone to transcription errors, and no easy way to compare historical data across months.

workflow: Manually updating the project's README or GitHub Pages with links to latest dev.to articles to keep the documentation in sync.
trigger: Publishing a new article on dev.to that should be referenced from the project's GitHub repo.
current_workaround: Editing the README.md directly, committing and pushing changes, or using a GitHub Action that fetches RSS but still requires manual setup.
consequence: README becomes stale, outdated links, and missed opportunities for cross-promotion.

target_role: team lead / manager of a dev.to publication
workflow: Coordinating multiple authors in a publication: managing permissions, approving drafts, and ensuring consistent branding without a proper workflow.
trigger: Onboarding a new writer or publishing a draft that needs review.
current_workaround: Using a shared spreadsheet to track authors, drafts, and publication status; manually adjusting permissions in the dev.to settings.
consequence: Permission errors, missed reviews, and inconsistent branding; heavy reliance on email and manual communication.
